narrative_purpose: Shows the first genuine kill strategy as different from clear-cutting: leave almost all ordinary forest standing, identify the rare sacred hubs across land and sea, and remove them together so their dependent regions become isolated.
subject: A high oblique view across forest, mountains, coast, and reef at night. Almost every ordinary tree remains intact. Seven rare luminous hub structures are distributed far apart: several willow-like sacred trees on land, a broad glowing fungal hub, and two rooted Spirit Trees under shallow sea. Each hub is encircled by a small dark targeting ring at the same moment; around the already dimming hubs, fine network links break and broad regions separate into disconnected pools of light while untouched ordinary forest remains standing.
scene: A moon-scale surgical attack map embedded in a real landscape, focusing on simultaneous removal of rare hubs rather than area burned.
camera: Very high three-quarter panorama spanning several biomes while keeping the seven hub targets individually legible.
light: Cool bioluminescent network light across the intact world, hubs brightest; sparse magenta rings mark only the targeted nodes, with no broad fire glow.
palette: Cool night landscape and cyan-teal hubs, rare magenta targeting accents, almost no amber because the strategy is surgical rather than incendiary.
style: Painterly speculative-biology map-landscape hybrid, natural forms rather than flat symbols.
detail_level: Crisp on each distinct hub and the severed links around it; ordinary forest recedes into haze.
composition: Seven targets spread across the full frame with dark air and water beside them for labels; disconnected light regions become readable without borders.
consistency_notes: Most biomass must remain untouched. The failure comes specifically from losing several rare high-connectivity hubs simultaneously across different biomes.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no continent-wide fire, no one giant central tree, no photographic satellite image, no glossy 3D render, no neon HUD
